summary: Reviewed the aiohttp 'sqli' training app (views, routes, DAOs, middlewares, app setup, templates, fixtures). All 6 findings were confirmed in the code at (or very near) their cited locations and are kept. The app runs every state-changing endpoint unauthenticated (routes.py has no auth on POST /students/, /courses/, /courses/{id}/review), so the SQL injection and stored XSS are reachable by anonymous users; the remaining findings (disabled CSRF middleware, unsalted MD5 password hashing, non-HttpOnly session cookie, and debug mode) are all accurate configuration/implementation facts. Nothing was dropped; line/severity values were only minor-adjusted where needed.

findings.title: Unauthenticated SQL injection in Student.create
findings.description: The INSERT query is built with Python %-string formatting of the attacker-supplied student name instead of a parameterized query, then passed to cur.execute(q) with no bound parameters (student.py:45). The value flows unvalidated from the unauthenticated POST /students/ handler (views.py:54-57, data['name'], no schema check; route registered with no auth at routes.py:14) directly into the SQL string. An attacker can submit a name like `x'); DROP TABLE students; --` to read or modify arbitrary data. Reachable by any anonymous user. Confirmed that every other DAO method (student.py:18, review.py:19-24, user.py:23-26/33-37) correctly uses bound parameters; this is the single string-formatted sink.
findings.evidence: q = ("INSERT INTO students (name) " "VALUES ('%(name)s')" % {'name': name}) -> cur.execute(q) ; source: views.students POST (views.py:54-57) -> Student.create(conn, data['name']); route POST /students/ at routes.py:14 has no authorize
findings.recommendation: Use a parameterized query: await cur.execute("INSERT INTO students (name) VALUES (%(name)s)", {'name': name}). Also enforce a schema on the input in the view.

findings.title: Stored XSS via globally disabled Jinja2 autoescaping
findings.description: aiohttp_jinja2 is configured with autoescape=False (app.py:35), so no template output is HTML-escaped. The unauthenticated POST /courses/{id}/review handler (views.py:111-131, route at routes.py:28-30) stores review_text verbatim via Review.create (review.py:28-36), which course.jinja2:22 renders as `{{ review.review_text }}` with no escaping filter. Any visitor to the course page then executes attacker JavaScript. The same disabled escaping also makes course.title/description (course.jinja2:9,14,15) and student.name (course.jinja2:49) injectable sinks. Combined with the httponly=False session cookie this enables session theft.
findings.evidence: setup_jinja(app, loader=..., context_processors=[...], autoescape=False) (app.py:33-35); sink: templates/course.jinja2:22 `{{ review.review_text }}`; source: views.review POST -> Review.create(conn, course_id, review_text)
findings.recommendation: Enable autoescaping (autoescape=select_autoescape(['jinja2','html']) or True) and explicitly mark only known-safe output. Do not rely on per-template escaping with it globally off.

findings.title: CSRF protection disabled application-wide
findings.description: A working CSRF middleware exists (middlewares.py:25-38) and a csrf_token is available to templates (utils/jinja2.py:8-16), but the middleware is commented out of the middleware chain (app.py:27, and it is not even imported at app.py:8), so no POST request's token is ever validated. All state-changing endpoints (POST /, /students/, /courses/, /students/{id}/evaluate/{course_id}, /courses/{id}/review, /logout/) accept forged cross-site requests. Because the session cookie is used ambiently, an attacker page can create students, courses, reviews, assign marks, or log the victim out on their behalf.
findings.evidence: middlewares=[session_middleware, # csrf_middleware, error_middleware] (app.py:25-29); csrf_middleware implemented in middlewares.py:25-38 but never imported/registered
findings.recommendation: Re-enable csrf_middleware in the middleware list (and import it), ensure token generation runs for GET forms, or use a maintained CSRF library.

findings.title: Unsalted MD5 used for password hashing
findings.description: Password verification compares the stored hash to a plain, unsalted MD5 of the supplied password (user.py:40-41); fixtures also seed pwd_hash with md5() (migrations/001-fixtures.sql:10-13). MD5 is fast and unsalted, so any disclosed users.pwd_hash column (e.g. via the SQL injection above) is trivially cracked with rainbow tables/brute force, and identical passwords yield identical hashes. The comparison (==) is also non-constant-time.
findings.evidence: return self.pwd_hash == md5(password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest() (user.py:41); fixtures: VALUES ('Super',...,md5('superadmin'),TRUE), ... md5('password') ... (001-fixtures.sql:10-13)
findings.recommendation: Use a slow, salted password hash (bcrypt/argon2/scrypt via passlib) and compare with the library's verify (constant-time). Migrate existing hashes.

findings.title: Session cookie set with HttpOnly disabled
findings.description: RedisStorage is created with httponly=False (middlewares.py:20), so the session identifier cookie is readable by client-side JavaScript. Together with the stored XSS from disabled autoescaping, an attacker can exfiltrate the session cookie via document.cookie and hijack authenticated (including admin) sessions. The cookie is also not marked Secure, allowing transmission over plain HTTP.
findings.recommendation: Use httponly=True (the default) and set secure=True so the session cookie is inaccessible to JS and only sent over HTTPS.

findings.title: aiohttp application started with debug mode enabled
findings.description: The Application is constructed with debug=True (app.py:23-24) and run.py sets logging to DEBUG (run.py:11). Debug mode increases verbosity and can surface internal details/warnings, which aids attackers in reconnaissance. This should never be enabled in production. Note: aiohttp's debug flag does not expose an interactive web debugger (unlike Flask/Django), so real-world impact is limited, hence low severity.
findings.recommendation: Disable debug (or drive it from configuration/environment so it defaults to False in production).
